Evolve the Admin Desktop into a multi-surface project by implementing the Rider-specific views and tiered access logic. Reuse existing Velo Modern components with role-based subset rendering.

**Phase 1: Component Porting**
- Extract React code from `stitch rider desktop view.zip` into `admin/src/components/rider/`.
- Support 5 new views: Member Profile, Pending HUD, Guest Conversion, Club Home, and Auth Suite.
- Use established CSS variables (`--brand-primary`, etc.).

- Implement Tier Detection (Guest, Initiated, Affiliated) in `useAppStore`.
- Wire Auth Suite to Supabase Magic Link.
- Gate Calendar/Routes behind Tier 3 (Affiliated) status.

**Phase 3: Subset Rendering**
- Update existing `CalendarGrid` and `RouteLibrary` to hide Edit/Create/Delete buttons for users with `member` role.

### Persona Decision Receipt:
- **The Architect:** Defined the `account_tenants` junction table (Amendment A-01) to support multi-membership and tiered RLS.
- **The Designer:** Mandated the "Quiet" professional pending banner and gallery-style guest conversion prompts.
- **The Engineer:** Implemented the `can_view_calendar` SQL utility to enforce conditional Tier 2 access.

data.description: After customizing ride geometry in RideBuilder, start_coords may not be persisting to the database at all. data.why: Interactive maps were broken for all users — ApiProjectMapError fired on every map load, showing a blank map placeholder. Hours were spent investigating GCP configuration (billing, referrer restrictions, API enablement) before discovering the root cause was wrong option names in the loader call.
data.description: The mapsLoader.ts singleton was calling setOptions() with camelCase option names (apiKey, version) instead of the correct names (key, v) defined in the APIOptions type. The loader converts camelCase to snake_case via a regex transform, so apiKey became api_key in the URL instead of the required key parameter. This caused ApiProjectMapError on every map load because Google Maps JS API could not authenticate the request, despite the key being valid and all GCP settings being correct.
data.what: Change setOptions({ apiKey, version }) to setOptions({ key, v }) in admin/src/lib/mapsLoader.ts
data.completion_summary: Fixed setOptions option names: apiKey→key, version→v
pitfalls: Do not use apiKey — the correct field name is key per APIOptions type
Do not use version — the correct field name is v per APIOptions type
Do not instantiate new Loader() — v2.0.2 removed the Loader class, use setOptions + importLibrary
setOptions is a one-time singleton — calling it twice is silently ignored; ensure it runs before any importLibrary call

data.why: Users upload a new photo expecting immediate visual feedback. Instead they see no change and assume the upload failed, despite the success confirmation. This erodes trust in the profile management flow.
data.description: Uploading a new profile photo via the Profile page returns a success toast and invalidates the my-profile React Query cache, but the avatar image in both the Profile page and the nav top-right does not visually update. Root cause: the avatar is always uploaded to the same storage path (uuid/avatar.jpg), so the Supabase public URL never changes between uploads. The browser caches the image at that URL and serves the stale version even after React re-renders with the same src. Fixed by appending a timestamp query param (?v=Date.now()) to the publicUrl before storing it in the accounts table, so each upload produces a unique URL that bypasses the browser cache.

data.why: Guests scanning a ride QR code got a server 404, and even when the page loaded, their RSVP was silently dropped with no feedback and their email discarded.
data.description:
Three compounding bugs broke the entire guest RSVP experience when a non-member scanned a ride QR code:

1. Vercel rewrite used (.*)  regex which is silently ignored — all /portal/* deep links returned HTTP 404 before the SPA loaded.
2. RLS bypass (dev_public_select_rides) was removed without a replacement, blocking anon reads on rides AND causing the participant_insert_policy WITH CHECK (ride_id IN SELECT id FROM rides) to silently fail for guests.
3. ToastContainer was only in admin Layout, not RiderLayout — RSVP confirmation toast never rendered for guest users.
4. Guest email was collected in the UI but never passed through handleJoin → joinRide → INSERT, and no email column existed in ride_participants.
data.what: Fix Vercel SPA routing, restore public RLS on rides, add ToastContainer to RiderLayout, thread email through the RSVP flow and add the column.
data.completion_summary: Fixed 4 compounding bugs in guest RSVP flow — all deployed to production.
pitfalls: Vercel (.*)  regex is silently ignored — always use :path* for SPA catch-alls
cleanUrls: true interferes with rewrite chains in subdirectory SPAs
participant_insert_policy uses ride_id IN (SELECT id FROM rides) — if rides are unreadable by anon, inserts silently fail
ToastContainer must be present in every layout that calls addToast
